{
 "path": "programs/task-5a7f4658.py",
 "content": "def transform(grid):
    # Decode the colored intersections of the regular lattice into cells:
    # a cell is colored when all four corner intersections agree.
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    line = max(set(v for row in grid for v in row), key=lambda v: sum(row.count(v) for row in grid))
    rows = [r for r in range(h) if sum(x == line for x in grid[r]) >= w * 0.8]
    cols = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == line for r in range(h)) >= h * 0.8]
    if len(rows) < 2 or len(cols) < 2:
        return grid
    # Restrict to the lattice span containing non-line intersection marks.
    pts = [(i,j) for i,r in enumerate(rows) for j,c in enumerate(cols) if grid[r][c] != line]
    if not pts:
        return [[line]]
    r0,r1 = min(i for i,j in pts), max(i for i,j in pts)
    c0,c1 = min(j for i,j in pts), max(j for i,j in pts)
    interior = max(set(v for row in grid for v in row if v != line), key=lambda v: sum(row.count(v) for row in grid))
    out=[]
    for i in range(r0,r1):
        row=[]
        for j in range(c0,c1):
            a,b=grid[rows[i]][cols[j]],grid[rows[i]][cols[j+1]]
            c,d=grid[rows[i+1]][cols[j]],grid[rows[i+1]][cols[j+1]]
            row.append(a if a==b==c==d and a!=line else interior)
        out.append(row)
    return out
"
}

{
 "path": "programs/task-5a7f4658.py",
 "content": "from collections import Counter

def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    # Grid rails are the regularly spaced rows/columns dominated by rail color.
    rowdom=[Counter(r).most_common(1)[0][0] for r in grid]
    cold=[]
    for c in range(w):
        cold.append(Counter(grid[r][c] for r in range(h)).most_common(1)[0][0])
    rail=Counter(rowdom+cold).most_common(1)[0][0]
    rows=[r for r in range(h) if sum(x==rail for x in grid[r])>=w*0.8]
    cols=[c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c]==rail for r in range(h))>=h*0.8]
    if len(rows)<2 or len(cols)<2: return grid
    marks=[(i,j) for i,r in enumerate(rows) for j,c in enumerate(cols) if grid[r][c]!=rail]
    if not marks: return [[rail]]
    r0,r1=min(i for i,j in marks),max(i for i,j in marks)
    c0,c1=min(j for i,j in marks),max(j for i,j in marks)
    fill=Counter(v for row in grid for v in row if v!=rail).most_common(1)[0][0]
    out=[]
    for i in range(r0,r1):
        line=[]
        for j in range(c0,c1):
            a,b=grid[rows[i]][cols[j]],grid[rows[i]][cols[j+1]]
            c,d=grid[rows[i+1]][cols[j]],grid[rows[i+1]][cols[j+1]]
            line.append(a if a==b==c==d and a!=rail else fill)
        out.append(line)
    return out
"
}

 "content": "from collections import Counter

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # The horizontal rails are the repeated full-width rows.
    rail_rows = [r for r, row in enumerate(grid) if len(set(row)) <= 2 and row.count(Counter(row).most_common(1)[0][0]) >= w-2]
    if len(rail_rows) < 2:
        return grid
    rail_color = Counter(grid[r][0] for r in rail_rows).most_common(1)[0][0]
    # Interior fill is the most common color away from the horizontal rails.
    nonrails = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) if r not in rail_rows for c in range(w)]
    fill = Counter(nonrails).most_common(1)[0][0]
    # Find internal vertical rails: columns that carry the rail color between
    # horizontal rails. Exclude the outer edge columns.
    cols = []
    for c in range(1, w-1):
        if all(grid[r][c] == rail_color for r in range(h) if r not in rail_rows):
            cols.append(c)
    # Only retain regularly spaced dividers; the outer left/right edges bound
    # the first and last cells.
    xs = [0] + cols + [w-1]
    # Remove columns that are not true dividers by requiring their coordinates
    # to recur as rail intersections and their intervals to be substantial.
    xs = [x for i,x in enumerate(xs) if i == 0 or i == len(xs)-1 or x in cols]
    out=[]
    for a,b in zip(rail_rows, rail_rows[1:]):
        row=[]
        for left,right in zip(xs, xs[1:]):
            corners=[grid[a][left],grid[a][right],grid[b][left],grid[b][right]]
            counts=Counter(corners)
            color,n=counts.most_common(1)[0]
            row.append(color if n >= 3 and color != rail_color else fill)
        out.append(row)
    return out
"
}

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Lattice rails are near-uniform complete rows and columns.
    row_candidates = [(r, Counter(row).most_common(1)[0][0]) for r, row in enumerate(grid)
                      if Counter(row).most_common(1)[0][1] >= w - 2]
    col_candidates = []
    for c in range(w):
        vals = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h)]
        if Counter(vals).most_common(1)[0][1] >= h - 2:
            col_candidates.append((c, Counter(vals).most_common(1)[0][0]))
    if len(row_candidates) < 2 or len(col_candidates) < 2:
        return grid
    rail = Counter([v for _, v in row_candidates] + [v for _, v in col_candidates]).most_common(1)[0][0]
    rows = [r for r, v in row_candidates if v == rail]
    cols = [c for c, v in col_candidates if v == rail]
    if len(rows) < 2 or len(cols) < 2:
        return grid
    # The color filling the large tiles is the most common value away from rails.
    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) if r not in rows for c in range(w) if c not in cols]
    fill = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0]
    marks = [(i, j) for i, r in enumerate(rows) for j, c in enumerate(cols)
             if grid[r][c] != rail]
    if not marks:
        return [[fill]]
    r0, r1 = min(i for i, _ in marks), max(i for i, _ in marks)
    c0, c1 = min(j for _, j in marks), max(j for _, j in marks)
    out = []
    for i in range(r0, r1):
        line = []
        for j in range(c0, c1):
            corners = [grid[rows[i]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i]][cols[j+1]],
                       grid[rows[i+1]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i+1]][cols[j+1]]]
            line.append(corners[0] if corners[0] != rail and all(x == corners[0] for x in corners) else fill)
        out.append(line)
    return out
"
}
